chunks: Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from al-Himyari, from Ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He has lied the one who claims that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is from a thing, or in a thing, or upon a thing.

key_terms.عَلَى شَيْءٍ: Upon a thing (resting upon a support or base)
key_terms.فِي شَيْءٍ: In a thing (contained within a location or container)
key_terms.مِنْ شَيْءٍ: From a thing (derived from or composed of parts/substance)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when God is said to be 'not in a thing' or 'from a thing'?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) serves as a concise theological axiom in Shia kalām, systematically negating spatial dimensions (jism) and physical location (makan) to refute anthropomorphism (tajsim). By denying that God is 'from,' 'in,' or 'on' anything, it establishes His absolute transcendence (tanzih) beyond the limitations of created matter and space. This narration is frequently cited by scholars like al-Kulayni and al-Saduq to demonstrate the pre-rational certainty of God's non-corporeal nature.
